title: Fuzzy Adaptive Tuning of a Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Variable-Strength Combinatorial Test Suite Generation
review_status: full-text audit complete; method, 30-run design, three configuration tables, best and mean suite-size outcomes, interval plots, runtime exclusion, stochasticity caveat, and future-work/venue status checked
sections_checked: Sections 5–6: Mamdani FPSO, baselines, benchmark configurations, 30-run design, runtime exclusion
Section 7: Tables 3–5 and 95% interval plots for best/mean suite size
Section 8: stochastic-run caveat and future work
venue_year_verified: IET book chapter, Swarm Intelligence Volume 3: Applications (2018); UMPSA institutional repository record lists pp. 1–21; arXiv v1 submitted 2018-10-13
evidence_note: FPSO adapts PSO inertia for variable-strength combinatorial test-suite generation. The experiment reports suite size only, not SUT fault detection or execution time; runtime is explicitly excluded due to differing implementations/environments. DPSO generally leads on minimum and mean suite size, though FPSO wins some mean comparisons. The authors say further empirical evaluation is warranted and warn that best stochastic-run outcomes may occur by chance.

title: Empirical Notes on the Interaction Between Continuous Kernel Fuzzing and Development
review_status: full-text audit complete; snapshot, four-kernel pending/closed distributions, Linux bug-type and commit-marker measures, regression, and all four stated limitations checked
sections_checked: Sections II–III: 2019-06-30 syzbot snapshot, units, methods, and measured distributions
Section III: pending-report medians, Linux time-to-fix, review/test markers, regression results
Section IV: conceptual, empirical, longitudinal, and methodological limitations
evidence_note: The exploratory four-kernel snapshot reports >800 unresolved crash reports, not necessarily distinct confirmed bugs; pending-report medians are 136/51/53/119 days for Linux/FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD, while closed Linux reports have median 38-day time-to-fix. Review/test status is inferred from commit-message markers. The study itself flags duplicate symptoms, false positives/non-reproducibility, single-snapshot scope, and cross-kernel comparability limits.

title: An Extensive Empirical Study on Evaluation Metrics for Combinatorial Interaction Testing
review_status: targeted full-text follow-up; full 90-page arXiv PDF checked for abstract/body sample counts, fault-set construction, metric-correlation results, metric saturation, and threats to validity; not independently replicated
sections_checked: Abstract/introduction and front matter: claimed 8 projects/32 scenarios vs body’s nine programs/36 scenarios; unresolved JACM 2018 and DOI placeholders
Sections 4.2–4.5: metric/fault-detection correlation design, SIR mutation faults and three real-fault program families
Sections 5.3–5.6 and 6: IMS/VCC/discrepancy results, VCC strength-1 saturation caveat, computational cost and validity threats
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-10-01; no peer-reviewed venue independently verified
evidence_note: This is material counterevidence to the broad idea that static combinatorial metrics have never been related to fault detection: the paper reports VCC as its best overall predictor and uses both verified mutation faults and historical developer-confirmed faults. However, the abstract says eight programs/32 scenarios while the body says nine/36, and the front matter carries JACM 2018/placeholder DOI text inconsistent with its 2026 arXiv date. Treat as an unreviewed lead until the version, dataset, and artifact can be reconciled; it does not evaluate FPSO itself.

title: SyzRetrospector: A Large-Scale Retrospective Study of Syzbot
review_status: targeted full-text follow-up; definitions, historical reconstruction design, 559-case cohort, 50-case manual validation, results, and stated exclusions/biases checked
sections_checked: Sections III–V: D1 hidden/unfindable and D2 revealed-but-not-found definitions and retrospective method
Sections VII–VIII: 1,159 candidate to 559 retrospectable cases, D1/D2 estimates, 50-case manual review
Section X: non-reproduction/build exclusions and upstream-only cohort bias
venue_year_verified: RAID 2025, pp. 92–105; arXiv v1 first submitted 2024-01-22
evidence_note: For 559 retrospectable upstream Linux bugs, the paper reports mean D1=331.17 days before the bug became findable by Syzbot and mean D2=73.94 days after revelation until discovery. A random 50-case manual check judged 44 revealing factors correct. Initial candidate pool was 1,159; non-reproducible/build-failing cases were excluded, and the authors say hard-to-reproduce cases likely cause D2 underestimation. This refines—not directly contradicts—the 2019 pending-report/time-to-fix study because it measures different life-cycle intervals and has a different Linux-only cohort.
